instructions: Start this about 7 hours before you want to bake. In a small bowl, stir the yeast, 1/3 cup lukewarm water and a pinch of the sugar. Leave it for about 30 minutes, until foamy.
Crush the mastiha and mahlepi with a pinch of the sugar in a mortar or small bowl.

In a small saucepan over low heat, warm the butter, the remaining sugar and 1/3 cup of the milk, stirring, until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves. Take the pan off the heat and let it cool until lukewarm.
Whisk 2 of the eggs into the lukewarm butter mixture, then stir in the yeast mixture.
Zest half the orange. In the bowl of a stand mixer, combine 2 2/3 cups of the flour, the crushed spices and the zest.
Add the wet mixture. Mix on low until combined, then on medium high for 10 to 15 minutes, until the dough pulls away from the bowl. It should be soft and a little sticky.
Cover the bowl and leave the dough in a warm place for 3 to 4 hours, until doubled.
Punch the dough down and cut it into 2 equal pieces. Cover them and rest for 20 minutes.
Dust the counter with some of the last 1/3 cup flour. Cut each piece into 3 ropes and roll them out. Braid the 3 ropes of each piece, and transfer the 2 braids to parchment lined baking sheets.
Cover the braids and leave them in a warm, draft free spot for 2 to 3 hours, until puffed.
Toward the end of the rise, heat the oven to 350°F.
Separate the last egg and beat the yolk with the last 1 tsp milk. Brush it over the braids and sprinkle on the sesame seeds.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until golden. Watch them near the end. They brown fast.
Cool the loaves completely. Keep one wrapped in a sealed bag at room temperature, where it keeps for several days. Wrap the other tightly and freeze it for up to 2 months.
advance_prep_notes: Start the dough about 7 hours ahead: it rises 3 to 4 hours, then the braids rise another 2 to 3.
method_notes: Mia Kouppa (the lead, 4.96 from 49 ratings) makes six loaves from a rich dough with mastiha and mahlepi; this is a third of it, so two loaves. My Greek Dish (4.65 from 893) agrees on the spices, orange zest, two long rises and a 350°F oven but uses fewer eggs, and adds a syrup that is left out here. Both top the loaves with almonds or sesame; almonds are left out to keep it nut free, and mahlepi is a cherry seed, not a nut. Prep time counts the rising.
